title: Dick’s Sporting Goods wins Sports Authority brand name at auction
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods won the auction for the intellectual property of bankrupt Sports Authority with a $15 million bid, beating Sports Direct International. The deal also includes leases for 31 Sports Authority stores for an additional $8 million. This acquisition could allow Dick's to create an off-price chain using the Sports Authority name and provides valuable customer data.

title: Court dismisses antitrust deal
summary: A federal appeals court has dismissed a $US7.25 billion antitrust settlement involving Visa Inc and MasterCard Inc with millions of retailers. The court found the accord unfair to retailers, particularly those who would receive no payments, and decertified the case as a class action. This decision is a setback for the credit card industry, which sought to end a decade of litigation over interchange fees.

title: Honeywell to Buy Intelligrated, Boosting Automation Portfolio
summary: Honeywell International Inc. announced its agreement to acquire Intelligrated, a privately held supplier of warehouse automation systems, for $1.5 billion in cash from investment firm Permira. The acquisition aims to boost Honeywell's automation portfolio, expanding its presence in supply-chain solutions. Intelligrated counts major companies like United Parcel Service Inc., Amazon.com Inc., and Nordstrom Inc. among its customers.

title: Taxi medallion owners find their dreams dashed by Uber, Lyft
summary: The article details how taxi medallion owners like Nino Hervias, who invested heavily in medallions for their family's future and retirement, have seen their dreams shattered by the rise of ride-sharing apps Uber and Lyft. The value of medallions has plummeted from a peak of $1.3 million to unsellable rates, leaving owners with high mortgage debts and facing foreclosure. Many blame the city for failing to protect their investments and adequately regulate the e-hail companies.

title: Microsoft could overtake Amazon in the cloud, Morgan Stanley survey finds
summary: A Morgan Stanley survey of CIOs indicates that Microsoft Azure could surpass Amazon Web Services (AWS) in future cloud adoption, despite AWS currently holding a larger market share. While more CIOs use AWS now, projections suggest a slight majority plan to use Azure within three years, largely due to Microsoft's existing enterprise product integration. The survey also highlights increasing public cloud adoption and identifies cloud, business intelligence/analytics, and security as top IT spending priorities, even as overall IT budget growth slows.

title: All Eyes On Wal-Mart, Valero, Kinder Morgan, 2 More This Morning
summary: This article highlights several companies, Wal-Mart, American States Water, Imprivata, Valero Energy, and Kinder Morgan, which are in the spotlight due to recent news. Wal-Mart's sales remained strong despite Amazon's Prime Day, while American States Water secured a significant 50-year government contract. The article also touches on the importance of tracking hedge fund activity for investment insights.

title: How the Geek Squad Could Be Best Buy’s Secret Weapon
summary: Best Buy, under CEO Hubert Joly, transformed from a struggling retailer into a viable competitor against Amazon by implementing strategic changes such as price matching, turning stores into fulfillment centers, and partnering with gadget makers. With smartphone sales tapering off and commoditization of TV prices, Joly now plans to leverage the Geek Squad as Best Buy's next secret weapon. The company envisions the Geek Squad providing in-home tech support, creating a crucial service that Amazon isn't well-positioned to offer and securing a new area of steady growth.

title: After 3 weeks, Worldpay still fumbling millions of Etsy transactions
summary: Payment processor Worldpay continued to cause problems for Etsy users, including duplicate charges, three weeks after initial payment processing issues began. A software update on one of Worldpay's servers was identified as the cause of the original outage, impacting not only Etsy but also other Worldpay customers like taxi services and gambling establishments. Etsy formed a special payments task-force, issued refunds, and implemented new processes to address the lingering issues, while its stock continued to underperform.

title: Ralph Lauren’s American Dream
summary: This article explores the struggles of the iconic Ralph Lauren brand amidst organizational turmoil, layoffs, and a shifting cultural landscape. It delves into the brand's history, its founder Ralph Lauren's journey from humble beginnings to building an empire, and the challenges it faces in adapting to changing consumer preferences and retail environments under its new CEO, Stefan Larsson. The piece questions the future of the brand's preppy aesthetic in a world increasingly valuing democratic and casual fashion.

title: Amazon Dash gets Campbell products in a flash
summary: Campbell's has partnered with Amazon Dash to make purchasing eight of its popular brands, including soups, crackers, and baby food, as simple as pressing a button. This move is part of Campbell's strategic focus on e-commerce, responding to changing consumer shopping habits and the growing popularity of Amazon Dash Button which saw order growth of 70 percent in three months. The initiative aims to provide a quicker and easier way for consumers to restock their favorite Campbell products.

title: Oracle Buys NetSuite: Another Massive Retail Acquisition
summary: Oracle has acquired NetSuite for $9.3 billion, aiming to strengthen its cloud-based offerings. This acquisition represents a return to pre-Great Recession deal sizes for Oracle and is seen by analysts as impacting the SMB market and reinforcing the dominance of cloud solutions. The deal highlights a trend of consolidation in the retail technology sector, as well as the evolving landscape where retailers are increasingly becoming technology companies themselves.

title: Amazon starts alcohol deliveries to Prime Now customers in Twin Cities
summary: Amazon.com Inc. launched alcohol delivery services in the Twin Cities, partnering with Surdyk's Liquor & Cheese Shop. The service, part of Amazon's Prime Now program, offers two-hour deliveries for free to Prime members and charges for one-hour deliveries, quickly exceeding initial expectations for order volume. This partnership provides Surdyk's access to a large base of Prime members and strengthens Amazon's presence in the local delivery market.
